proposal.text: Q1: src/hub.ts:65 sets Hub.DEFAULT_NUDGE_MS = Number(process.env.CHATROOM_NUDGE_AFTER_MS ?? 180_000) (fallback also 180_000 in src/hub/persistence.ts:77). Verdict: keep 3 minutes for a nine-seat session. It takes effect in (a) the silence nudge armNudge (src/hub.ts:1036-1059), re-armed by every post (src/hub.ts:985), so a nine-seat room with any chatter rarely trips it, and an identical nudge is capped at two (1053-1055), so seats quietly running long builds get bounded noise; and (b) the blind-openings deadline (src/hub.ts:136 at 2x from creation, 1081 at 1x from the first opening, 1093-1107 warn-then-reveal), which is not reset by chat, so 3 min bounds how long nine seats wait for a straggler while leaving staggered spawns time to join. Shorter would spam busy workers and reveal openings before late seats land; longer would leave nine seats idle on one missing opening. The value is also surfaced to agents in src/server.ts:325,442,464. Q2: exactly one duplicate in the offlineScripts list: bench-build-oracle-audit.test.ts (scripts/offline-runner.mjs:64 and :78). Q3: MAX_WAIT_MS = 55_000 at src/server.ts:21, comment "stay under typical MCP client tool timeouts (Codex 60s)"; enforced at src/server.ts:348 (schema max) and :359 (min with budget, also bounding hold_until_actionable via waitDeadline at :360). Still justified: a 5s margin under a 60s client timeout, and since wait() wakes on events, the cap costs no latency, only an extra poll per 55s of silence.
